predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contractual End Date Overrun Without Formal Amendment May Create Legal and Commercial Exposure
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project timeline extends 7 weeks beyond the contractual end date of September 11, 2026, with critical activities including PAT, regression testing, deployment, and hypercare planned through October 30, 2026. No formal contract amendment has been executed to document the revised end date, payment terms, scope additions, or governance arrangements, creating significant legal, financial, and operational uncertainty.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Original 16-week baseline underestimated the complexity of AI/ML development, integration, quality assurance, and deployment activities. PAT and regression testing were added after project initiation but were not incorporated into a formal contract amendment. Execution model shifted from phase-gate to agile with iterative feedback, extending timeline without commercial realignment.
triggerConditions: Project activities continue beyond September 11, 2026 without executed contract amendment
Payment milestone for UAT Sign Off (10%, $24,200) reaches due date without revised payment schedule
Deployment and Hypercare milestones (15%, $36,300 combined) become due outside contractual coverage period

potentialImpact.contractual: Operating without valid contractual coverage creates liability gaps, warranty ambiguity, and potential disputes over payment obligations for work performed after September 11, 2026
potentialImpact.financial: Payment terms for $60,500 (25% of contract value) covering UAT, Deployment, and Hypercare milestones are undefined beyond contract end date, creating revenue recognition risk for vendor and payment obligation uncertainty for client
potentialImpact.governance: Governance framework, escalation procedures, and decision authority may not apply beyond contractual term, weakening project control and issue resolution capability during critical deployment phase

predictedRisks.reasoning: This risk is highly likely to materialize because project activities are already planned through October 30, 2026, extending 7 weeks beyond the September 11, 2026 contractual end date, yet no formal amendment has been documented in either the SOW or WSR. Historical evidence from the same client program shows that unplanned PAT and regression expansion previously created contractual ambiguity that was never structurally resolved. Current project intelligence confirms that PAT (through September 18), regression (through October 9), and go-live (October 10-16) all fall outside the contract term. The risk is relevant to the upcoming PAT and deployment phases where payment milestones totaling 25% of contract value become due without defined commercial terms.
monitoringIndicators: Contract amendment execution status and signature completion date
Revised payment milestone schedule alignment with actual project timeline
Formal governance framework extension confirmation documented in steering committee minutes

projectIndicators: Contract end date: September 11, 2026 vs. planned completion: October 30, 2026 (7-week gap)
WSR project timeline shows PAT through September 18, regression through October 9, go-live October 10-16, hypercare through October 30
Extension analysis states: 'No formal contract amendment or extension documented in SOW or WSR'
Contractual impact severity rated HIGH with risks including 'No formal extension agreement documented' and 'Payment terms beyond September 11, 2026 not defined'
historicalReferences: Historical risk R02: 'Regression testing and extended PAT duration were added after project initiation and are not part of the original SOW'
Historical risk marked 'Mitigated' but mitigation effectiveness rated LOW with no evidence of formal amendment or baseline revision
Historical recurrence likelihood: Very High, with evidence that 'Current project exhibits explicit PAT and regression expansion beyond baseline'

actions: Execute formal contract amendment documenting revised end date (October 30, 2026), updated payment milestone schedule aligned to PAT/regression/deployment phases, and extended governance framework coverage through hypercare completion

Finalize and obtain executive sign-off on revised payment terms for UAT Sign Off (10%, $24,200), Deployment (5%, $12,100), and Hypercare (10%, $24,200) milestones with updated due dates reflecting actual project timeline

recommendations.Governance: Convene joint steering committee session by August 20 to approve contract amendment terms, confirm extended liability and warranty coverage through October 30, and formalize decision authority for post-September 11 activities
recommendations.Commercial: Document cost impact assessment for 7-week extension, clarify whether $242,000 contract value covers extended effort or requires adjustment, and establish change order process for any additional scope beyond amended baseline
recommendations.Risk Management: Establish monthly contract compliance review cadence through October 30 to monitor adherence to amended terms and proactively identify any further timeline or scope variances requiring commercial adjustment

predictedRisks.responseRationale: Historical risk R02 documented identical contractual ambiguity when regression and extended PAT were added outside the original SOW, marked mitigated but never formally resolved through baseline amendment. That unresolved condition has recurred with 7-week extension beyond contract end date. Immediate contract amendment is the only durable mitigation to eliminate legal exposure and payment uncertainty for 25% of contract value ($60,500) due beyond September 11.

A significant percentage of bugs are UI/UX-related usability issues, and bugs are being created for in-flight functionalities, indicating incomplete development or insufficient unit testing. This accumulating technical debt may prevent timely PAT entry on August 31 or extend the PAT phase beyond the September 18 code freeze date.

Heavy reliance on manual validation given the growing number of form validation rules creates testing bottlenecks. UI/UX issues suggest insufficient upfront design or usability validation. Iterative PAT early access feedback is generating additional bugs and enhancement requests that are being incorporated into subsequent sprints, extending the defect lifecycle.
